label: An approval request from Klaxon: a write action that runs only if a person approves it.

alert.name: MoneyCheckFailed
alert.summary: The money check failed 2 of its 5 invariants: posted_exactly_once (7 findings), matches_provider (8 findings). By its count, our ledger is $493.23 ahead of the provider's balance.

plan.change: redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER naive -> idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS dead_letter (unchanged)
plan.undo: going back to LEDGER_HANDLER=naive would deploy a known-bad setting: Klaxon will not; a person can, by hand

diagnosis.hypothesis: At 09:06:30 ledger-consumer was redeployed with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. This handler appears to book every Kafka record it reads without deduplicating by event_id. The provider resends webhooks until they are acknowledged, so one event can land on provider-events more than once, at different offsets. Each copy was booked as a new ledger transaction. That gives 7 events posted 2 or 3 times (posted_exactly_once failed). It also puts provider_clearing $493.23 ahead of the provider (matches_provider failed). Duplicate payment.succeeded events inflate the balance. The duplicate refund.succeeded for pay_000217 leaves that payment at 1 cent against the provider's 2456. The ledger stays balanced because each duplicate is a full double-entry transaction. Our payments and refunds still match the provider, so the damage is confined to the ledger. Still open: the handler that ran before this deploy, and whether it was idempotent, was not confirmed.

evidence.shows: Symptom reproduced. posted_exactly_once failed: 7 events posted 2 or 3 times, e.g. evt_000308 three times. matches_provider is off by +$493.23. ledger_balanced passed, and payments and refunds match the provider.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 09:06:30Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, about 17 seconds before the alert. No other service changed after 09:04:46.
evt_000308 was posted 3 times between 09:06:44 and 09:06:46, from provider-events/0 offsets 100, 101 and 103. These are redelivered copies of one event, each booked again.
evt_000251 was posted twice at 09:06:31, just after the deploy, from provider-events/2 offsets 73 and 76. Same pattern: no dedupe by event_id.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to the settings it ran before the 09:06:30 deploy, presumably an idempotent handler that dedupes by event_id. Then repair the ledger separately: reverse the extra transactions the money check lists (e.g. 255, 266, 272, 273, 297, plus the extras for evt_000298 and evt_000308). Then rerun money_check.

diagnosis.blast_radius: Recreating ledger-consumer pauses ledger booking briefly. Events wait in Kafka and are booked after the restart, so lag rises for a short time. payment-confirmer is unaffected. Duplicate entries already booked stay until a separate data repair. The previous handler's name was not confirmed from the deploy log.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the restored settings misbehave, stop ledger-consumer and let events queue in Kafka. Only as a last resort redeploy LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, since it keeps double-booking.
